assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn deaminase chemistry into a programmable tool that changes single nucleotides without double-strand breaks, with direct consequences for genome maintenance, disease models and therapy. The conceptual step (fusing a nucleobase deaminase to a Cas9 nickase, then evolving an adenine deaminase that does not exist in nature) is original and chemically explicit.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly decisive as senior inventor; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, including the evolved TadA) were the lead experimentalists. Kondo and Nishida's parallel Target-AID work is real but the supplied credit favors the Liu trio; a fair three-person split is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is now emerging and many independent laboratories have reproduced and extended the editors, so the result is robust. Timing is reasonable, though the 2020 CRISPR prize may make the committee cautious about a second genome-editing award.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views base editing as an extension of an already honored discovery (CRISPR-Cas9).
Fair recognition of Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work.
Long-term safety data (off-target deamination) are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by reversible-terminator chemistry changed the economics of reading DNA and underlies modern genomics, cancer and aging research. The underlying chemistry (reversibly blocked, labeled nucleotides and polymerase incorporation on a surface) is nucleotide chemistry of the kind I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis approach and are the clearest pair. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454), Ju and Mayer have legitimate competing claims to different NGS technologies, so the scope of the prize would need careful definition.
assessment.maturity: Transformative and in universal use for roughly two decades, with unquestioned reproducibility. Recognition is well overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The 'NGS' umbrella covers several distinct chemistries (reversible terminators, pyrosequencing, sequencing by ligation), making attribution contested.
Sanger and Gilbert's 1980 prize may be viewed as having covered DNA sequencing broadly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity to trigger ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of targets expands what is druggable, and the molecular glue story (thalidomide acting through cereblon) connects well with protein-chemistry mechanism. Clinical-stage degraders give the work biomedical weight.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed VHL-based degraders and ternary-complex structural mechanism. Handa, Ito and others made the cereblon discovery for glue degraders, so a three-person prize would leave out an important mechanistic branch.
assessment.maturity: Field is moving fast with many independent groups and clinical trials, but approvals of a PROTAC drug are still pending, which makes it slightly early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet; clinical validation is incomplete.
Splitting credit between heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues (cereblon biology).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made siRNA and mRNA medicines deliverable, as shown by Onpattro and the COVID-19 vaccines. The key design principle, a pH-dependent ionizable lipid that is neutral in circulation and charged in endosomes, is a clear chemical idea with enormous impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's Vancouver group developed the formulation and microfluidic mixing concepts, with Hope and Madden as early core inventors. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer made important lipid-library and optimization contributions, so allocation of credit is a genuine difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Validated by hundreds of millions of vaccine doses and an approved siRNA drug, so maturity is high. The 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modifications does not cover the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine recognition may make the committee hesitant.
Credit among the Vancouver group, MacLachlan and the MIT/Alnylam teams is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is one of the central metalloenzymes of life, reducing N2 to ammonia with a unique FeMo-cofactor. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and the cofactor with its interstitial carbide, plus mechanistic work, convert a biological process into a defined chemical reaction.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first structures and cofactor architecture) and Einsle (high-resolution structure showing the central light atom) are decisive for structure; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism and genetics. Ribbe's work on cofactor biosynthesis is also important, so the three-name selection excludes substantial contributors.
assessment.maturity: Structures were independently confirmed over decades, but the catalytic mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is still not fully settled, which makes the interpretation only partly mature.
uncertainties: The full catalytic mechanism remains debated.
Multiple strong contributors (Dean, Ribbe) are excluded by the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry-based proteomics lets one measure thousands of proteins and modifications and has become the analytical backbone of molecular biology. The methodological advances (shotgun proteomics, SRM and quantitative labeling) are broad and important for any biochemist.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are widely viewed as the central figures; Hunt, Gygi and Heck have strong claims, which makes the allocation crowded and arguable. The 2002 Chemistry prize already honored soft ionization for biomolecular MS.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature and reproduced everywhere. Timing is fine, but the fragmentation of the field into several contributions weakens a clean statement.
uncertainties: Crowded credit across at least six candidates.
Possible perception of overlap with the 2002 prize for biomolecular mass spectrometry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids through orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs gives chemists direct control over protein chemistry in living cells, with wide use in probes, photocrosslinking and therapeutics. It is a general tool for biologists built on a defined chemical principle.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach, Wang made the first in vivo demonstrations in E. coli and eukaryotes, and Chin extended it to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama have additional claims, so the allocation is plausible but imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups and in broad use, though clinical translation is limited and the more ambitious genome-recoded organisms are still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the impact as sufficiently broad beyond specialist labs.
Credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's discovery of covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket, and earlier analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics, turned a target regarded as undruggable into one with approved drugs. It is a clear case of chemical mechanism enabling a biological and medical advance.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is clean for a sole laureate on KRAS G12C, although the clinical drugs were developed at Amgen and Mirati building on his tethering approach. Pairing with the kinase chemical genetics adds a second idea that might need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adagrasib are approved and independent groups have confirmed the mechanism. Recognition is timely, though clinical benefit is incomplete due to resistance.
uncertainties: Dependence of the clinical drugs on later industrial optimization.
Resistance to G12C inhibitors limits the long-term clinical story.
Compound discovery (KRAS plus kinase chemical genetics).
